title: Create a local keyed table
summary: A DynamoDB table declares its key attributes.
introduction: A DynamoDB table declares its key attributes. Your task: Check that the table key names match the item design.
learningObjectives: Check that the table key names match the item design.
Explain the example for create a local keyed table

blocks.text: A DynamoDB table declares its key attributes. Other item fields do not need to be declared as table columns.

Use DynamoDB Local and the AWS CLI or SDK in a separate practice project. Point every command at http://localhost:8000. Low-level JSON examples show request bodies; provide them to the matching CLI command or SDK method.

blocks.code: aws dynamodb create-table --table-name cma-books --attribute-definitions AttributeName=reader,AttributeType=S AttributeName=book,AttributeType=S --key-schema AttributeName=reader,KeyType=HASH AttributeName=book,KeyType=RANGE --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST --endpoint-url http://localhost:8000
blocks.title: Create a local keyed table

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `--endpoint-url` points this CLI call to DynamoDB Local. Keeping it explicit avoids accidentally using a configured cloud endpoint.

blocks.text: DynamoDB Local creates the sample table with reader and book keys.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Keep the local endpoint option. Omitting it can target a real configured AWS account instead.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Check that the table key names match the item design.
